To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 350 μm emission of local LIRGs is dominated by dust grains with emissivity indices of β ≈ 1.6 and temperatures of T_d = (39.4 ±7.9) K, and the dust temperature and emissivity index are correlated in a way that cannot be explained by the dust temperature and luminosity alone.
the dust temperature, T_d, and emissivity index, β, are correlated with each other, with the correlation being described by T_d ~ (9.86×10^9) ^{(1/(4.65 + β))}.

the 350 μm emission of local LIRGs is best described by a single-temperature modified blackbody model with a median dust temperature of 39.4 K, an emissivity index of 1.6, and a median FIR luminosity of 10^(11) L⊙, and that the observed T_d-β relation can be explained by variations in the ISM grain properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical conditions of the dust in LIRGs, which is important for understanding the star formation process in the local universe.

two main aspects of the dust emission properties in local LIRGs: 1) the temperature dependence of the grain emissivity and 2) the dust temperature distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the local LIRGs are characterized by a single temperature, a single emissivity index, and a single FIR luminosity.

the observed inverse T_d- β correlation for the local LRG sample is a result of the combination of the intrinsic interdependence of these two parameters, as well the variation of the grain emissivity index in the ISM.

the local LIRGs are not consistent with a single dust temperature or a single grain size distribution, which is in contrast to the findings from the Herschel Space Observatory (Herschel) for a large sample of distant LIRGs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the local LIRGs have dust temperatures and FIR luminosites similar to those of the local ULIRGs, and their SEDs are well described by single-temperature models with β = 1 - 2.
the dust temperature is an important parameter in determining the grain emissivity index.
the observed T_d-β relation is a result of the combined effects of the dust temperature and emissivity index, as well as the variations of grain properties in the ISM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature and emissivity index are not two independent physical parameters in SED fitting.
the T_d-β relation can be used as a diagnostic tool to constrain the grain emissivity index and dust temperature in the ISM.

, in addition to the dust temperature and luminosity, the grain emissivity index is an important physical parameter in the SED modeling, which should be taken into account when studying the dust temperature and the dust mass.
